text:
maria: quick q — can we add a top-level "binding.namespace" to rollout metadata to capture tenant-scoped model bindings? trying to avoid lots of tenant-specific label hacks :thinking:

alex: why not use labels? namespaces feels heavier. what's the concrete problem?

maria: labels are fine for UI/ops, but we need a deterministic client resolver rule. clients need to answer: is this pin visible to me (tenant X) without calling control-plane. labels are freeform. namespace would be a first-class field with clear semantics.

sam: +1 for explicit field. smaller surface, easier validation. worried about multi-tenant fallthroughs — if namespace is null should we treat as global?

kai: proposal: three modes: "global" | "tenant:<id>" | "namespace:<logical>". default empty = global. clients must do exact-match check before falling back. that way we avoid ambiguous label semantics.

maria: rough schema snippet i banged out: 
```json
{
  "rollout_id": "string",
  "model_ref": "string",
  "binding": {
    "type": "soft|hard",
    "namespace": "global|tenant:<id>|namespace:<name>",
    "expires_at": "rfc3339|null"
  },
  "constraints": {
    "region": ["us-west1"],
    "capacity_tier": "dedicated|hosted"
  }
}
```

alex: schema looks fine. couple thoughts: 1) avoid embedding tenant ids in metadata the control plane returns to arbitrary clients (PII / enumeration risk). 2) what about tenant overrides for private deployments?

sam: good pickup. we can encode namespace as hashed token or opaque id in public endpoints. control plane would map tenant-id -> opaque namespace id for public APIs. internal/private APIs (private control-plane) can use clear text.

kai: about rollouts and precedence: if a request matches multiple pins (global + tenant-scoped), client should prefer most-specific: tenant > namespace > global. Also prefer non-expired. we should document tie-breaker: newest created win, then lexical model_ref as determinism.

maria: migration plan idea: 1) introduce "binding.namespace" as optional string. 2) advertise opaque namespace tokens in public model catalog. 3) run a 2-week compatibility window where clients still consult labels but prefer new field when present. 4) after adoption window, enforce clients to use namespace matching check.

alex: ops note — telemetry: emit events when a request matched a tenant-scoped pin vs global pin. add a new metric: pin_match_scope{global,tenant,namespace}.

ops-bot: deploy scheduled: feature-flag rollout for "binding.namespace" field in control-plane API on Tue 03:00 UTC.

sam: edge case: what if tenant pins a model and then revokes it but global pin still exists? we should not let revoked tenant pin create a silent fallback to global if the tenant explicitly removed their binding. recommend explicit "disabled: true" flag for tenant pins to preserve intent.
